reason: Selected multi-turn coding evaluation supports measuring process compliance independently of functional output.

candidates.title: Audit procedural constraints throughout multi-turn coding
candidates.rule: When evaluating coding agents, check active process and repository constraints after each turn as well as final functional correctness, especially after requirements change.
candidates.passage: updating existing constraints is notably harder than adding new ones.
candidates.location: Sections 4.3–4.4, constraint sources and evaluation reliability
candidates.finding: MTAC-IFBench finds procedural compliance deteriorates across turns and remains weaker than functional success. Harness choice changes results, and superseded constraints create a different challenge from newly added ones. The suggested audit workflow is inferred.
workloads: MTAC-IFBench multi-turn coding under Claude Code and OpenCode
candidates.conditions: Average instances contain about seven turns and ninety-one constraints. Evaluation combines scripts with judge agents and sampled human checks.
candidates.limitations: Judge agreement is imperfect, especially for functional checks. Repository-policy versus user-constraint comparisons need not isolate placement causally. Synthetic benchmark constraints may differ from ordinary development workflows.
candidates.validation_test: Build a turn-wise active-constraint checklist including replacements; score function and procedure separately under pinned harness versions. Measure stale-rule violations, omissions and evaluation disagreement.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
